title: Finite Hamiltonian carre-du-champ comparison for physical-coordinate likelihood gradients
question: Does the physical-coordinate conditional form track the Hamiltonian-derived kinetic carre-du-champ on the actual Q3 likelihood gradients, after the coordinate-only potential terms are removed by commutation?
method: Reconstruct the finite Q3 Gibbs state, every split-history prefix and both history adjoints from the R-399 fixture.
For every oriented collar row, form the conditional coordinate law pi and the actual likelihood multiplier f=q_prefix/p_prefix.
Compute D_q(f) with oscillator coordinate spacings and E_kin(f)=(2 chi)^(-1) Tr(diag(pi)[p,F]^*[p,F]) in the q basis.
Check a coordinate-only onsite potential and spatial Q3 bond commutator, then report the finite E_kin/D_q interval without treating it as a uniform constant.
Repeat both orientations, source/history signs, split orders, prefixes and adjoints; use a momentum-to-coordinate hostile mutation and a non-importing independent lane, then compile Lean R402.
finding: The finite Hamiltonian-derived kinetic form is nonnegative on all 71680 conditional rows, and the coordinate-only potential commutator residual is zero on every declared system.  The primary lane passes 5410/5410, the independent lane 1815/1815, the hostile lane 4/4, the integrated verifier 33/33 and Lean R402 compiles.  Of 71680 rows, 57680 have nonzero coordinate form and their E_kin/D_q ratios range from 1.0087179063711833 to 11.074061483593928.  The q-for-p hostile mutation gives zero while a selected genuine kinetic row is positive.
decision_reason: R-402 advances R-401 from a proposed coordinate metric to a finite interface tied to the actual Q3 kinetic generator: coordinate potentials commute with F=f(q), while the p commutator is nonzero on actual history likelihoods.  The broad finite ratio interval and finite oscillator boundary prevent an analytic comparison claim.  The route remains advanced only at T0 finite-interface level.

adversarial_review.check: D_q and E_kin are computed as separate quadratic forms and only their finite ratio is reported.
A site potential and a Q3 bond are checked to commute with F=f(q); non-coordinate observables remain outside scope.
Finite oscillator matrices are bounded and the observed ratio is not promoted to a cutoff-independent constant.
Both collars, source/history signs, split orders, prefixes and adjoints are included and rebuilt independently.
Replacing p by q makes the commutator vanish while the genuine kinetic form is positive on a selected row.
No uniform comparison, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure follows.

next_action: Prove or refute an analytic two-sided E_kin versus D_q comparison on a cutoff-independent Hamiltonian common core, with source-, volume-, cutoff-, phase-, orientation- and shape-uniform constants; then repeat the phase-conditioned and increasing-exhaustion stress before combining with R-399.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Hamiltonian carre-du-champ comparison only.  It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or shape-uniform comparison, no invariant common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: A finite kinetic commutator form and a finite coordinate Dirichlet form are different quadratic forms.  Their observed ratio is a diagnostic, not an analytic comparison theorem or a Q3 real-time locality result.
